scope: One recursive CTE with one nonrecursive signed integer literal, a single self-reference and one signed literal increment. The continuation compares the current column against a signed literal with a strict inequality. The outer query reads the current column once or more under explicit resolved result names.
open: More than one recursive column, source or branch
Additional anchors, arithmetic roles, comparisons or predicates
Recursive and dependent definitions in the same WITH list
SEARCH, CYCLE and additional query clauses

RecursiveSeries.role: A query whose recursive input is its single-column working relation
invariants: The continuation is a strict comparison of the current value to the boundary.
Less-than uses a positive increment and greater-than uses a negative increment.
The nonempty ordered result has at most 1024 fields and every reference selects slot zero.
RecursiveSeries.meaning: Admit the initial row. While the current value passes the continuation test, add the signed increment in the native integer domain and admit the following row. UNION ALL preserves admissions. UNION removes already admitted rows. Each output position reads the same resolved slot under its own name.
RecursiveSeries.sql: Emit one WITH RECURSIVE definition using canonical relation and column names. Emit the selected UNION policy, signed native literals, and the continuation with its original operand roles. Quote each consumer output name.

analysis: Verify that the recursive and consuming inputs resolve to the exact same CTE definition by binding identity. Resolve the step, condition and consumer references against the corresponding one-slot layout. An original external table with the same spelling is irrelevant to the verified local binding.
observations: Ordered output names and native type tags
Multiset of typed rows, including no-step and one-step cases and repeated reads
Whether each continued row satisfies the signed step rule

finite.completeness: Observe the exact product of start, increment, boundary and quantifier from directly constructed values with comparison determined by the sign of the increment.

negative: Advance away from the continuation boundary
Step reference to a different relation
trust: Native integer evaluation and anchor field types are interpreted under the fixed language profile.
The independent interpreter evaluates short walks from the model. Arithmetic overflow, configured recursion exhaustion and execution failures belong to runtime evaluation.

nativeTypes.mysql: The signed integer anchor of the recursive UNION yields a LONGLONG field in the pinned profiles.
nativeTypes.postgres: The signed integer anchor and step use the builtin int4 operations and yield int4.
nativeTypes.addedBoundaries: Observe the smallest and largest signed 32-bit initial values, zero, and both UNION quantifiers.

changeFromRevision1: MySQL 8.4 reported LONGLONG where the initial evaluator predicted LONG from the ordinary derived-field rule. This revision keeps exact native type comparison, adds explicit anchor metadata and tests boundary values. The finite product, seed, timeout and fault requirements are unchanged.
